Only this one test class exists; the only failures are the 3 above, and they reflect genuine bugs rather than flawed assertions. I'm confident in the test suite as written.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/ExtendedBufferedReaderAgentTest.java` with 30 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering happy paths, boundaries, and error cases (construction, `read()`/`read(char[],int,int)`, `peek()`, `readLine()`, `mark()`/`reset()`, `close()`, and byte-tracking with an encoder, including malformed/surrogate input).

27 tests pass. 3 fail, and each failure points to a real bug in `ExtendedBufferedReader`, not a test error:

1. **`testReadAtEofDoesNotAdvancePosition`** — `read()` increments `position` unconditionally (`src/main/java/.../ExtendedBufferedReader.java:217`), even when it returns `EOF`. Calling `read()` repeatedly past end-of-stream keeps growing `getPosition()`, contradicting the documented semantics ("counting characters... read so far").

2. **`testEmptyStreamSingleReadLineNumberStaysZero`** — On a completely empty stream, the very first `read()` call increments `lineNumber` from 0 to 1, because `lastChar` starts as `UNDEFINED` (not `CR`/`LF`/`EOF`), so the EOF-triggers-newline branch in `read()` (line 210) fires spuriously. An empty stream should report 0 lines.

3. **`testBulkReadLineCountingMatchesSingleCharReadAcrossSmallBuffers`** — `read()` and `read(char[], int, int)` disagree on line counting for the same input: the single-char `read()` counts a trailing partial line (content with no terminator before EOF) as a line, but `read(char[], int, int)` never applies that rule (its EOF branch at line 242-244 just sets `lastChar = EOF` without touching `lineNumber`). This produces different `getLineNumber()` results depending solely on which read method the caller used.
